title: Uniform purity of a geometric constituent by two-point curves
statement:
Fix a prime power $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an isomorphism $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$, as in [def-weil-punctual-weights]. Let $X_0$ be a nonempty smooth geometrically connected affine $k_0$-scheme of relative dimension at least one, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $\mathcal G$ be a classical lisse $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves; def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] that is $\iota$-real [def-wf-iota-real]. Suppose
$$0=\mathcal G_0\subset\mathcal G_1\subset\cdots\subset\mathcal G_r=\mathcal G$$
is a finite filtration by lisse Weil subsheaves whose quotients $\mathcal S_j=\mathcal G_j/\mathcal G_{j-1}$ are nonzero and have geometrically irreducible underlying local systems. There exist real numbers $w_j$ such that every $\mathcal S_j$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w_j$ on all of $X_0$.

More precisely, fix any closed point $x_*\in X_0$. For every other closed point $x$ and chosen geometric lifts of $x_*,x$, there are $m\ge1$ and a smooth geometrically connected affine curve $C_m\hookrightarrow X_0\times_{k_0}\mathbf F_{q^m}$ whose geometric image contains both lifts, such that the pullbacks of all $\mathcal S_j$ are geometrically irreducible and punctually pure. The restriction of $\mathcal G$ to $C_m$ is real. For any eigenvalue $\alpha\ne0$ of $\mathcal S_j$ at $x_*$, every such curve purity weight is the same number
$$w_j=2\log_{q_{x_*}}|\iota(\alpha)|.$$
If $z_*,z\in C_m$ lie over $x_*,x$, with residue degrees $e=[\kappa(z_*):\kappa(x_*)]$ and $f=[\kappa(z):\kappa(x)]$, the local eigenvalues are the corresponding $e$th and $f$th powers and their residue sizes are $q_{x_*}^e,q_x^f$. For each eigenvalue $\beta$ at $x$, one has $|\iota(\beta)|=q_x^{w_j/2}$. The simultaneous assertion permits $r=0$ and $x=x_*$; no semisimplicity of $\mathcal G$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-zl-curve-testing-irreducibility] to the two chosen lifts, as a singleton when equal, and the whole finite family of quotients. Apply [lem-zl-geometric-closed-curve-smooth-model] to its closed geometric curve. This gives one smooth geometrically connected affine model over some $k_m$ through both lifts, with closed points under them and all geometric quotient restrictions irreducible. Both lemmas permit an empty family.

proof.text: Apply [lem-zl-curve-restriction-filtration-spectrum] to this model and the supplied filtration. It gives the classical lisse restricted filtration with exactly the restricted quotients, the same common-stage operators, reality of the total sheaf, and the residue-degree power formulas with multiplicities at all closed points.

proof.text: By [lem-zl-geometric-quotient-weil-composition-series], the nonzero geometrically irreducible restricted quotients are constituents of the real lisse sheaf on this curve. Apply [thm-rp-real-lisse-purity-affine] over $k_m$ to obtain their punctual purity. These results apply to the actual filtration without a splitting or semisimplicity assumption.

proof.text: Fix $j$. Let the test collection consist of the models just obtained as $x$ and the choices vary. Steps 1-3 verify all three hypotheses of [lem-zl-anchored-pure-curve-criterion]: coverage includes the anchor itself, restrictions are pure, and their spectra and residue sizes have the required powers. It supplies $w_j$, its formula for every anchor eigenvalue, independence of every curve purity weight, and purity at every closed point. The additional-curve clause proves the same independence for any further pure test curve. Do this for each member of the finite family. When $r=0$ no criterion is needed: Steps 1-2 already supply the simultaneous curve, reality and local formulas. This proves every clause of the unchanged statement.
